subject: System Design
title: Partitioning and Sharding
description: Learn Partitioning and Sharding in one minute.

hook.text: One database holds 10 TB. Queries are slow. Splitting it across 10 machines makes each one fast again.

buildup.text: Sharding splits data into partitions. Each shard holds a subset, like users A-M on shard 1, N-Z on shard 2.

discovery.text: A good shard key distributes data evenly. A bad one creates hot spots that overload one shard.

twist.text: Cross-shard queries are expensive. If user A's data needs user B's data on another shard, joins get complex.

climax.text: Sharding enables massive scale but adds complexity in routing, rebalancing, and cross-shard operations.

punchline.text: Split data to scale — but choose the split wisely.

quiz.question: What is a hot spot in sharding?
options: One shard receiving disproportionately more traffic
The fastest shard in the cluster
